d.x: [T]he landlord, starting up at the well known sound, cried, “Odd's niggers! there is the commodore with his company, as sure as I live!”

Any mammal in the order Perissodactyla, including horses and other equids, rhinoceroses, and tapirs.

odd-toed ungulate.e: From odd-toed (as a translation of the taxonomic name, translingual Perissodactyla, from Ancient Greek περισσός (perissós, “odd in number”) + δάκτυλος (dáktulos, “toe”)) + ungulate.

d.g: A civil parish in Cheshire East district, Cheshire, England.

Odd Rode.e: Rode was recorded in the Domesday Book, possibly from Old English rodu (“clearing”). The origin of the affix Odd is not known.
